transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-21 09:00 PT
Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Emily Chu (Redwood SE), Carlos Vega (Redwood CSM); Mark Davis (CTO, StratusLink), Priya Rao (Security Lead), Nina Osei (Infra Eng), Tom Keller (Product)

---
Summary (auto): Short discovery on security posture and hosting options. Customer needs clarity on BYOK, audit logs, SOC2/ISO scope, and SSO. Preferences: start Hosted evaluation but may move to Dedicated/Private for keys and data residency.

Topics: SOC2, ISO, SSO SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS/HSM, data retention, hosted vs dedicated vs private

Transcript Body:
[00:00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll give a quick agenda — intro, high level sec posture, then dive into keys and hosting. Mark, you want to kick with where you stand?
[00:00:15] Mark: Sure yeah thanks Jordan. So basically we're evaluating Redwood for a couple of customer facing features. Main blockers from our side are compliance — SOC2 and ISO — and also we need customer-managed keys, like BYOK, because some of our contracts require it.
[00:00:30] Priya: And just to add, we need audit logs exported to our Splunk instance, retention at least two years, and SSO via SAML with SCIM provisioning.
[00:00:40] Emily: Great — thanks Priya. Quick note, Redwood has both hosted and dedicated options; Hosted is quickest but for BYOK and HSM we've seen customers pick Dedicated or Private. I'll explain tradeoffs in a minute.
[00:00:55] Nina: Question — are the logs we get real-time or batched? We want near real-time for incident response.
[00:01:05] Emily: You can stream audit logs; they support syslog/S3 export and we've built connectors for Splunk. Some customers pull asynchronously but latency is usually low — seconds to minutes depending on throughput.
[00:01:20] Tom: When you say BYOK, do you mean we can bring our AWS KMS key or an HSM? We use an HSM backed KMS for some regulated customers.
[00:01:30] Jordan: Yes, good Q. Redwood supports customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private deployments; Hosted has a BYOK path but that often requires additional compliance gating — we can share details. Emily, do you want to outline the KMS options?
[00:01:42] Emily: Yeah — rough breakdown: Hosted: Redwood-managed keys by default, with limited BYOK for enterprise with controls; Dedicated: customer KMS integration supported, you can rotate keys and we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and external HSM via KMIP in many cases; Private: full customer control, keys never leave customer VPC/HSM. There are some caveats around model caching and tokenization where we keep ephemeral caches but encrypted.
[00:02:05] Priya: Sorry, "ephemeral caches" — do you mean KV cache? We can't have plaintext model context stored in Redwood-managed infra.
[00:02:12] Emily: Right — KV cache. We encrypt cached segments at rest and for Dedicated we can configure that encryption to use your KMS. For Hosted we encrypt too but with Redwood-managed KMS unless BYOK is provisioned on the enterprise agreement. There can be tradeoffs in latency if the KMS is in another region.
[00:02:30] Mark: What's the SOC2 scope? We need Type II with system description that includes inference endpoints and telemetry.
[00:02:38] Jordan: We have SOC2 Type II covering our hosted API and control plane; I'll send the report after this call. Emily, meanwhile, items to flag for them?
[00:02:46] Emily: The SOC2 covers our control environment and incident response, but Dedicated/Private deployments shift some scope to the customer — e.g., network controls in a VPC. For ISO 27001, we maintain a cert for our control plane, but customers with strict ISO requirements often prefer Private to own more of the scope.
[00:03:05] Priya: So if we pick Dedicated, can you still attest on the same SOC2 scope or is that not covered?
[00:03:12] Emily: The SOC2 will note the managed services we provide; however certain infrastructure controls in Dedicated may be 'customer managed' and so you would need to include those in your own scope. We can provide control mappings and an SOC2 carve-out explanation.
[00:03:26] Tom: About SSO — we use Okta, SAML, and SCIM for provisioning. What's the flow?
[00:03:33] Jordan: We support SSO via SAML and SCIM provisioning for user accounts and RBAC. Emily, walk through the role mapping?
[00:03:40] Emily: Sure. You can map SAML assertions to roles in Redwood: admin, billing, developer, read-only. We also have service accounts for programmatic access with token rotation. SCIM will auto-provision users into the right groups. We also support SCIM filtering for groups.
[00:03:56] Nina: Do you support SCIM push for groups so we don't have to manage manually?
[00:04:02] Emily: Yes, full push support for groups and attributes. We'll share a sample Okta app config.
[00:04:10] Mark: Audit logs — we need immutable logs and the ability to export them to our SIEM and retain two years. Is that doable with Hosted?
[00:04:19] Emily: Hosted can export logs to S3 with lifecycle rules or stream to your SIEM; we can set retention policies on the storage side. For immutability, Dedicated/Private gives you more deterministic control — you can own the S3 bucket or SIEM ingest. Hosted will meet many customers' needs but if you need contractual guarantees about retention and immutability, we typically recommend Dedicated or Private.
[00:04:40] Priya: Encryption in transit AND at rest, plus key rotation policy — do you have rotation logs?
[00:04:46] Emily: Yes. We support TLS 1.2+/TLS 1.3 for transit; at rest is AES-256. KMS key rotation events are logged and surfaced in audit logs. If you use your KMS, you will see rotation events in your KMS logs.
[00:05:00] Mark: Any performance penalty when using BYOK across regions?
[00:05:05] Emily: Potentially. KMS calls for encryption/decryption add latency, but we mitigate by caching DEKs and minimizing round trips. If KMS endpoint is cross-region, it could add tens of milliseconds. For low-latency SLAs we can recommend co-located keys or Dedicated in same region.
[00:05:22] Tom: Pricing — is Dedicated a large step up?
[00:05:25] Jordan: It's a step up, yes — Dedicated includes reserved GPU pools and the enterprise networking/KMS integrations. Carlos will send a pilot quote.
[00:05:33] Carlos: I'll get you a number with a 90-day pilot option and options for burst capacity.
[00:05:36] Nina: One technical nit: how do you handle pingbacks for data deletion requests? We have GDPR requirements to purge logs/contexts for certain customers.
[00:05:46] Emily: We support deletion APIs for customer data in Hosted, and for Dedicated/Private you can enforce deletion in your VPC. We also keep a data retention config per tenant to comply with requests.
[00:05:58] Priya: Ok good. A couple of follow ups — can you show KMS integration in a deep dive? We'd like to see an HSM demonstration.
[00:06:06] Jordan: Absolutely. Proposed technical deep dive with Emily and a solutions engineer for 06/03. I'll send a calendar invite.
[00:06:12] Mark: Cool. If you could also send the SOC2 doc and a brief control mapping table to our compliance team that'd help us speed decisioning.
[00:06:20] Jordan: Will do. Also Emily will attach the SAML/SCIM sample config and the log export patterns. Carlos will attach pricing.
[00:06:28] Tom: Any red flags we should be aware of?
[00:06:30] Emily: Only that Hosted requires enterprise gating for BYOK and strict residency; Dedicated/Private removes most of that friction but has lead time. Also some advanced features like model-level caching encryption require configuration.
[00:06:45] Priya: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[00:06:48] Jordan: Great — recap: Jordan send SOC2 + ISO notes; Emily send SAML/SCIM guide and KMS technical notes; Carlos send pilot pricing; Nina and Priya to confirm retention & SIEM specifics; schedule deep dive for 06/03. Any final q's?
[00:06:59] Mark: None. Thanks.
[00:07:02] Jordan: Thanks all, we'll follow up by end of week.
